title: Pricing experiment runbook and enterprise security-questionnaire triggering guidelines
creator: Emma Zhang
description:
Summary: Define a lightweight, repeatable runbook for pricing and packaging experiments that interacts with enterprise contract approval and the security-questionnaire (SQ) workflow. The goal is to reduce time-to-decision for discount experiments while keeping finance and legal guardrails intact and ensuring high-risk customers trigger an SQ and escalated approval path.

Background: We frequently run ad-hoc discounts and packaging pilots for enterprise prospects (Dedicated/Private customers) which creates inconsistent outcomes: finance sees revenue leakage, sales rep experience is uneven, and legal/infosec occasionally receive late SQs. This ticket creates a single source of truth: an experiment runbook + gating rules that map experiment variants to approval lanes and SQ triggers.

Objectives:
- Provide a step-by-step experiment runbook for PM/RevOps/Sales to run pricing tests (design, control/treatment, sizing, metrics, rollout, rollback).
- Define discount authority lattice (who can approve what discount % by ARR/type and when Finance/Legal must sign off).
- Define deterministic rules that auto-trigger an SQ or escalate to Legal based on product footprint, data classification, and proposed contract terms.
- Ensure experiment telemetry is captured and visible in Console and the Pricing dashboard for retrospective evaluation.

Scope:
- Applies to enterprise deals (Dedicated, Private) and any packaging experiments that change committed capacity, data residency, or custom SLAs.
- Does NOT change list prices; this is an operational governance layer for exceptions and experiments.

Proposal (high level):
1) Experiment runbook steps: hypothesis -> kpi definition (unit economics, churn, conversion) -> sample selection -> control/treatment sizing -> approval checklist -> monitoring -> retrospective + decision. Include standard templates for experiment spec and an approved PRD template.
2) Discount authority lattice: 0-10%: AE manager approval; 10-25%: Sales Director + RevOps; >25% or multi-year/commitment: VP Sales + Finance + Legal. Separate caps for Marketplace vs Direct, and special handling for Dedicated capacity (because of GPU reservation cost impact).
3) SQ trigger rules (deterministic): if customer requests data residency, on-prem deployment, or annual contract > $350k OR requests deletion/retention modifications -> auto-create SQ workflow and notify Legal/Security. Include a lightweight SQ risk score that maps to discount caps (higher risk -> lower autonomous discount).
4) Packaging experiment guardrails: avoid concurrently testing seat-based and usage-based pricing on the same segments; limit concurrent active experiments to 3 per region/model family to avoid signal collision.
5) Telemetry & dashboards: require experiment ID embedded in sales contract metadata and Redwood Console route so rollout/latency/cost metrics can be correlated back to experiment variants.

Trade-offs considered:
- Speed vs control: tighter approval slows down reps but reduces revenue leakage. Proposed compromise: introduce fast-path approvals for low-risk experiments (<=10% discount, no infra changes).
- Centralized governance vs local autonomy: too centralized makes pilots slow; we instead use an authority lattice + required experiment tagging to balance autonomy with traceability.
- SQ automation complexity: fully automated SQ scoring is ideal but high effort. We start with deterministic rules (low lift) and iterate toward a scorecard-based automation.

Acceptance criteria (see field below) ensure we have artifacts, templates, and tech hooks before rolling to Sales.

Out-of-scope for this ticket: global pricebook update and changes to published list prices (handled in separate pricebook consolidation work).
acceptance_criteria: Experiment runbook doc published in Confluence with templates (spec + retrospective template)
Discount authority lattice published and circulated to Sales/RevOps/Finance/Legal
SQ triggering rules implemented as a checklist and integrated into the deal intake flow (Sales CRM metadata + one-click SQ creation)
Experiment tagging implemented in contract metadata and visible in pricing dashboard (end-to-end telemetry for metrics)
Pilot run: at least 2 live experiments following the runbook and producing measurable results within 8 weeks
